## Purpose and Entry Point
ani-cli is a Bash-based terminal application for searching, selecting, streaming, and downloading anime scraped from HiAnime. The executable implementation is the repository-root script at `ani-cli`; its user-facing interface and options are documented in `README.md` and the Unix manual page `ani-cli.1`.

## Runtime Model
The application runs in a Unix-compatible shell, including Git Bash on Windows and Termux on Android. It is intentionally a single-script architecture: orchestration, scraping, interactive selection, URL extraction, playback, download, and update behavior are concentrated in `ani-cli`. This makes shell command availability and platform behavior a primary operational boundary.

## Discovery and Selection Pipeline
The core flow begins from CLI arguments or an interactive search, retrieves and parses HiAnime content, then presents titles and episodes through `fzf`. Text extraction and request handling rely on shell utilities such as `curl`, `grep`, and `sed`; Cloudflare-compatible access may require `curl-impersonate`. The single script `ani-cli` owns this scrape-to-selection control flow.

## Playback Boundary
After an episode/provider stream is resolved, ani-cli delegates media handling to an external player rather than embedding playback. `mpv` is the main target; IINA is the macOS-compatible mpv replacement, and VLC is an optional alternative. Player invocation must carry stream metadata such as the required referrer, notably on Android. Optional intro/outro skipping is delegated through mpv’s Lua integration to external ani-skip tooling. Relevant user contract: `README.md`, `ani-cli`.

## Download Boundary
For `-d` download operations, the script hands stream acquisition to `yt-dlp`, with `ffmpeg` as a fallback for m3u8 content. Download location is controlled externally through `ANI_CLI_DOWNLOAD_DIR`; episode-range selection supports bulk downloading. The downloader/player dependency boundary keeps media protocol handling outside the Bash implementation. Core path: `ani-cli`.

## Distribution and Self-Maintenance
The root script is installed directly by source-based instructions and packaged by OS ecosystems. `Formula/ani-cli.rb` provides the Homebrew formula. Self-update behavior (`-U`) depends on Git/network retrieval and `patch`, so updates are an operational capability of the executable rather than a separate release client. `ani-cli.1` is the packaged/manual-facing CLI specification.

## Automation and Governance
GitHub Actions provide repository maintenance automation rather than runtime functionality: `inverse-ani.yml` and `inverse-md.yml` likely validate synchronization or inversions between the script and docs, while `version.yml` governs version-related checks. Contribution and ownership controls reside in `.github/CODEOWNERS`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, and workflow definitions under `.github/workflows/`.
